reasoning: A cool-blue accent is a relationship and perceptible role, not a coverage percentage. A neutral foreground badge carrying a clear blue check could satisfy the brief without a dominant blue field.
Transparent negative space is distinct from an opaque intentional foreground plate. Mechanical alpha counts cannot decide subject intent; corrected transparency uses visual evidence.
Asymmetrical check arms need not have unequal lengths: unequal angle, position, thickness or curvature can preserve qualitative asymmetry. Actual recognizability is the required outcome.

At 16x16, economical connected clusters and clear negative space serve quick success recognition. Their exact thickness, edge shading and backing are expert choices. A short-left/long-right plain-blue glyph is a good option, not a universal requirement.
